lane: T8 — Repair: dead complete/fail control, watchdog workspace, memory.dir override, memory merge order

findingsAddressed.title: the Detail tab's complete/fail taps could never succeed (anonymous panel tap vs owner-only tool)
findingsAddressed.fix: REMOVED the control, not the rule. `createTeamPanelActions` no longer publishes `complete`/`fail`, the Detail tab no longer renders them, and a `callout` says settling belongs to the owning member. `agent_teams_task` keeps its owner-only gate untouched (the finding's 'do NOT widen owner-only' direction).
findingsAddressed.whyThisShape: a tap carries no agent, so every alternative either widened the gate or faked an identity; hiding a dead control is the honest repair the verifier's own direction lists first

findingsAddressed.title: hold/resume could land in a workspace root that is not the panel's session root
findingsAddressed.fix: REMOVED the taps and made the Watchdog tab read-only, with copy naming where the action lives. The panel no longer routes a MUTATION through a tool whose exec has no session (`session-watchdog-hold`/`-resume` resolve their root from DSH_WORKSPACE_ROOT → cwd).
findingsAddressed.whyThisShape: the two sanctioned alternatives (hold/resume on the `mpdWatchdog` service, or a workspace-bound exec) live in the watchdog package and the adapter's `executeTool`, both outside this repair's write scope; leaving a tap that can write to the wrong store was not acceptable

findingsAddressed.title: the Memory tab ignored `memory.dir` and read the wrong store
findingsAddressed.fix: `readMemoryStore(workspace, now, scope)` now resolves `<workspace>/<memory.dir or ".mpd">/memory/agents/<slug>/…`, and `registerDshGoPanel` receives the scope from the mounted `mpdConfig` (`memory.dir`, `memory.agentSlug`) through `index.ts`. The GLOBAL store stays out of the tab by declaration: the caption says it reads THIS agent's workspace entries.
findingsAddressed.test: test/dshgo-panels-v2.test.ts — `memory.dir` moves the store; the default `.mpd` is then ignored

findingsAddressed.title: the Memory tab merged every agent slug, so another agent's entries could show
findingsAddressed.fix: the reader now walks ONE slug — the memory row's own rule, mirrored in `memorySlugOf` (explicit `memory.agentSlug`, else `agent-<workspace name>`) — and the caption states the ordering (newest by write time) so it cannot be mistaken for the tool's filename order.
findingsAddressed.test: test/dshgo-panels-v2.test.ts — a sibling agent's entry never leaks in; an explicit agentSlug selects that agent

findingsAddressed.title: legacy reflection.json keys showed 0/0
findingsAddressed.fix: the reader now falls back to `reflected_completed_steps` / `steps_since_last_successful_reflection`, mirroring the memory row's own compatibility bound; the current names still win.
findingsAddressed.test: test/dshgo-panels-v2.test.ts — legacy keys are read; current names take precedence
